data.hypothesis: The valid (32,8) and (32,16) mappings measured 3.473813 µs and 3.474453 µs, respectively, while (32,4) and (64,2) were slower than the 3.581547 µs baseline. Since these results do not show a monotonic relationship between Y block extent and latency, this candidate tests (32,2): it keeps each warp on adjacent X outputs at fixed Y/Z but increases the CTA count to see whether smaller CTAs offset their scheduling cost. No speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: This 64³ direct-global stencil; use as evidence that CTA shape effects are not monotonic in the measured candidates, not as a general GPU rule.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid (32,8) and (32,16) candidates had nearly equal measured means, while (32,4) and (64,2) did not beat the baseline. The observed measurements do not isolate a winning block-shape mechanism.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the new (32,2) mapping with the official correctness checks and repeated full-run timing before drawing conclusions.

data.notes: This is one launch-geometry experiment: only the block/grid Y mapping changes from the selected (32,16) parent. The controller should validate signed varying inputs, including independent endpoint values, and perform official timing; no new validation or timing is claimed here.
transformations: Change the launch from block (32,16,1), grid (2,4,64) to block (32,2,1), grid (2,32,64), retaining one output per thread and adjacent-X warps at fixed Y/Z.

Keep direct global loads, all eight Y-neighbors and supplied coefficients, the exact add/subtract-63 boundary rule (preserving in-range 63), and full output coverage without scratch use or input modification.
